understanding.title: Understanding Before Changing
understanding.content1: Most systems aren't greenfield. They're production systems with history, constraints, and business-critical behavior.
understanding.content2: Before making changes, I focus on understanding how the system behaves today, which workflows matter most, and where assumptions are undocumented.

behavior.title: Behavior Over Elegance
behavior.content1: Correctness and stability matter more than elegance.
behavior.content2: Refactoring without understanding behavior often creates subtle regressions that are expensive to detect and fix. Clean code matters when it supports reliability, clarity, and long-term maintainability.

refactoring.title: Refactoring Safely and Incrementally
refactoring.content: I treat refactoring as a controlled process:
refactoring.item3: Prefer small, reversible steps over large rewrites
refactoring.item4: Improve the system without disrupting production

ai.title: Using AI as a Supportive Tool
ai.content1: I use modern AI tools to reduce mechanical overhead and accelerate feedback, especially when exploring complex or unfamiliar codebases.
ai.content2: Examples include improving navigation through large systems, validating edge cases, drafting initial tests or documentation, and speeding up investigation cycles.
ai.content3: AI is a supportive tool, not a decision-maker. Responsibility for the final solution always remains with me.

experience.title: Experience Beyond the CV
experience.intro: Not all meaningful work fits into a one-page resume. Across product roles and consulting work, I've contributed to a wide range of systems, often already in production, undocumented, or constrained by legacy choices. Rather than listing clients, this page describes the kinds of environments I've worked in and how I approach them.

experience.title: Experience
experience.subtitle: Practical experience with real systems, not just ideal ones
experience.intro: Most of my professional experience has been working on existing production systems: often internal tools, CRMs, dashboards, and operational platforms that had already accumulated complexity over time. This includes both product roles and consulting work, where I was brought in to extend, stabilize, refactor, or unblock systems that were already in active use. Below is an overview of the kinds of environments I've worked in and the responsibilities I typically take on.

existingSystems.title: Working with Production Systems
existingSystems.intro: I have extensive experience joining projects after initial development, where systems already have:
existingSystems.item4: Technical debt accumulated under delivery pressure
existingSystems.role: In these environments, my role is usually to:
existingSystems.roleItem2: Identify high-risk areas before making changes
existingSystems.roleItem3: Improve reliability and maintainability without disrupting production

backendSystems.title: Backend and Data-Driven Systems
backendSystems.intro: A large portion of my work has been backend-focused, especially on data-driven internal systems where correctness and consistency matter more than visual polish. This includes:
backendSystems.item2: Business logic implemented across services and databases
backendSystems.item3: Working directly with relational databases and stored procedures
backendSystems.item4: Reasoning about data behavior over time and across workflows

internalTools.title: Internal Tools, CRMs, and Dashboards
internalTools.intro: Rather than public-facing marketing sites, most of my experience is with internal products used daily by operational teams. Typical characteristics of these systems:
internalTools.item4: Requirements that prioritize accuracy and predictability over aesthetics
internalTools.closing: I've built and maintained UIs that are tailored to specific operational needs, focusing on clarity, efficiency, and correctness rather than visual flair.

refactoring.title: Refactoring, Stabilization, and Ongoing Improvement
refactoring.intro: I'm often involved in work that includes:
refactoring.item2: Improving structure and readability without large rewrites
refactoring.item3: Introducing tests and documentation into existing systems
refactoring.item4: Debugging subtle production issues and edge cases
refactoring.closing: Rather than "rewrite everything" approaches, I focus on safe, controlled improvements that align with business constraints and team capacity.

constraints.title: Working Under Constraints
constraints.intro: Many of the systems I've worked on had real limitations, such as:
constraints.item1: Legacy runtimes or frameworks that could not be upgraded easily
constraints.item4: Dependencies on external or third-party systems
constraints.closing: I'm comfortable making pragmatic trade-offs in these situations and communicating them clearly, both technically and to non-technical stakeholders.

collaboration.title: Collaboration and Responsibility
collaboration.intro: Across teams and projects, I've often taken responsibility for:
collaboration.item1: Owning complex parts of the system
collaboration.item2: Supporting teammates by sharing context and reasoning
collaboration.item4: Leaving systems in a state that others can maintain with confidence
collaboration.closing: While I enjoy mentoring and knowledge sharing, my primary focus is always on delivering reliable, maintainable systems that teams can depend on.

approach.title: Engineering Mindset & Professional Approach
approach.subtitle: A focus on clarity, risk reduction, and long-term system health.
approach.intro: I approach software engineering with a focus on clarity, risk reduction, and long-term system health. My work is shaped less by trends and more by responsibility to real users, real data, and real production systems. This mindset is the foundation behind every role I take on.

principle1.title: Understand Before You Change
principle1.content: Before writing new code, I prioritize understanding:
items: How the system behaves in production
Which parts are fragile or business-critical
Why things were built the way they were
principle1.closing: This avoids breaking hidden dependencies and allows changes to be intentional and safe, not reactive.

principle2.title: Stability Over Elegance
principle2.content: Clean code matters — but correct behavior matters more.
principle2.closing: Refactoring is done incrementally, backed by tests or safeguards, never as a risky rewrite.

principle3.title: Work With Reality, Not Ideals
principle3.content: Most of my experience is with live systems:
principle3.closing: I'm comfortable improving systems as they are, not waiting for perfect conditions.

principle4.title: Incremental Improvement Beats Big Rewrites
principle4.content: Large rewrites are expensive and risky. I prefer:
principle4.closing: This keeps production stable while steadily raising quality.

principle5.title: Ownership Means Leaving Things Better
items: Making systems easier to reason about
Reducing cognitive load for the next developer
Adding clarity through structure, naming, and documentation

principle6.title: Backend & Data First Thinking
principle6.content: My strength is in backend-heavy, data-driven systems, where:
principle6.closing: Dashboards, CRMs, APIs, internal tools — systems where mistakes have real consequences.

principle7.title: AI as an Accelerator, Not a Crutch
principle7.closing: But responsibility for correctness, architecture, and decisions always stays with me.

benefitsTeams.title: How This Benefits Teams
benefitsTeams.content: Teams I work with get someone who:
items: Brings calm, structured reasoning into complex systems
Helps others understand why things work, not just how

inShort.title: In Short
inShort.content:
I'm not driven by hype or novelty.

I'm driven by:
items: Code that can be safely changed
Teams that can move forward without fear
inShort.closing: That mindset has guided my experience — and it's what I bring to every role.
